title: A pro-etale covering of a w-contractible affine has a section
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ the affine scheme [def-weil-affine-spectrum] [def-pc-scheme], in the universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Suppose every faithfully flat weakly etale ring map $A\to B$ [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map] [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra] admits a ring homomorphism $r:B\to A$ with $r\circ(A\to B)=\mathrm{id}_A$. For every pro-etale covering family $\{f_i:T_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-covering] indexed within these universes, let $p:\coprod_{i\in I}T_i\to T$ be the morphism induced by the $f_i$ from the scheme coproduct [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Then there is a morphism of schemes $\sigma:T\to\coprod_{i\in I}T_i$ such that $p\circ\sigma=\mathrm{id}_T$.

source.place: Tag 098F, lemma-w-contractible-proetale-cover, forward implication proof: refine by a finite affine standard covering using Tag 098D, lemma-proetale-affine, split its coproduct, then compose with the refinement map to the original coproduct. Tag 0981, definition-w-contractible.

proof.text: Apply the covering definition to the affine open $T\subseteq T$. It gives a finite set $J$, indices $i(j)\in I$, and affine open subschemes $U_j\subseteq T_{i(j)}$ such that $T=\bigcup_{j\in J}f_{i(j)}(U_j)$. Write $e_j:U_j\to T_{i(j)}$ for the inclusions and $g_j=f_{i(j)}\circ e_j$. Each $f_{i(j)}$ is weakly etale by the covering definition. To see that $g_j$ is weakly etale, apply the source-locality equivalence to the two-member open cover of $T_{i(j)}$ consisting of $e_j$ and its identity: its forward implication gives the assertion. This is the explicit finite affine refinement of Tag 098D. Repeated indices are allowed, and no image of a weakly etale morphism is assumed open. All selected opens and the finite index set stay in the supplied universes.

source.place: Tag 098D, lemma-proetale-affine, and Tag 098F, forward implication; more-morphisms.tex Tag 094S for restrictions

proof.text: Choose rings $B_j$ and affine identifications $U_j\simeq\operatorname{Spec}B_j$. Form $Q=\coprod_{j\in J}U_j$ with coprojections $c_j$, and let $q:Q\to T$ be induced by the $g_j$. Transporting the finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum isomorphism through these identifications gives $Q\simeq\operatorname{Spec}B$, where $B=\prod_{j\in J}B_j$. The coprojections are open immersions whose images cover $Q$, and $q\circ c_j=g_j$. Thus the reverse implication of source locality makes $q$ weakly etale. Its image contains every $g_j(U_j)$, whose union is $T$ by step 1, so $q$ is surjective. For $J=\varnothing$, $B$ is the zero ring and $Q$ is the empty scheme; step 1 forces $T$ empty. In particular this is a finite affine coproduct, never an assertion that an infinite product spectrum is a scheme coproduct.

source.place: Tag 098F, forward implication: the finite coproduct is an affine scheme and its map is surjective weakly etale; schemes.tex Tag 01I5 and more-morphisms.tex Tag 094S

proof.text: Under $Q\simeq\operatorname{Spec}B$, write $q=\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ for the unique ring map $\varphi:A\to B$, using affine-spectrum full faithfulness. Since a weakly etale morphism is flat, the flat-affine equivalence makes $\varphi$ flat. Surjectivity of $q$ and the flat-surjective-spectrum criterion then make $\varphi$ faithfully flat. The ring weakly-etale convention says precisely that $\varphi$ is weakly etale when $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ is, so it satisfies the other hypothesis of the item as well. Apply the supplied splitting hypothesis to obtain $r:B\to A$ with $r\circ\varphi=\mathrm{id}_A$. Contravariant functoriality of the affine spectrum turns $r$ into $s:T\to Q$ and the ring identity into $q\circ s=\mathrm{id}_T$. This also works for the zero ring; no nonemptiness assumption is needed.

source.place: Tag 098F, forward implication and Tag 0981, definition-w-contractible; morphisms.tex Tag 01U5 and algebra.tex Tag 00HQ

proof.text: Let $P=\coprod_{i\in I}T_i$ and let $d_i:T_i\to P$ be its coprojections. The maps $d_{i(j)}\circ e_j:U_j\to P$ induce $h:Q\to P$. On every summand, $(p\circ h)\circ c_j=f_{i(j)}\circ e_j=g_j=q\circ c_j$. Uniqueness in the coproduct mapping property gives $p\circ h=q$. Put $\sigma=h\circ s$. Then $p\circ\sigma=(p\circ h)\circ s=q\circ s=\mathrm{id}_T$, as required. If the covering family is empty, step 1 forces $T$ empty and the same coproduct uniqueness gives the identity. The construction only requires the small coproduct already in the statement, and makes no coefficient-category or base-change identification.
